66974-virginia-s-ranch-neighbors.title: Virginia S Ranch Neighbors
66974-virginia-s-ranch-neighbors.creator: Grace May North
66974-virginia-s-ranch-neighbors.description: A book by Grace May North. The older girl smiled but shook her sunny head. “No need to wish for that these days, dear. Life in Arizona is not nearly as thrilling as it is in the city of New York, if one can believe the newspapers.”

arxiv-2211-11061.title: Deep learning delay coordinate dynamics for chaotic attractors from partial observable data
arxiv-2211-11061.creator: Charles D. Young, Michael D. Graham
arxiv-2211-11061.description: Abstract A common problem in time series analysis is to predict dynamics with only scalar or partial observations of the underlying dynamical system. For data on a smooth compact manifold, Takens theorem proves a time delayed embedding of the partial state is diffeomorphic to the attractor, although for chaotic and highly nonlinear systems learning these delay coordinate mappings is challenging.

arxiv-2302-00479.title: Characterising Solutions of Anomalous Cancellation
arxiv-2302-00479.creator: Satvik Saha, Sohom Gupta, Sayan Dutta, Sourin Chatterjee
arxiv-2302-00479.description: Abstract Anomalous cancellation of fractions is a mathematically inaccurate method where cancelling the common digits of the numerator and denominator correctly reduces it. While it appears to be accidentally successful, the property of anomalous cancellation is intricately connected to the number of digits of the denominator as well as the base in which the fraction is represented.

arxiv-2308-15347.title: Masquerade: Simple and Lightweight Transaction Reordering Mitigation in Blockchains
arxiv-2308-15347.creator: Arti Vedula, Shaileshh Bojja Venkatakrishnan, Abhishek Gupta
arxiv-2308-15347.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arti Vedula, Shaileshh Bojja Venkatakrishnan, Abhishek Gupta. Blockchains offer strong security gurarantees, but cannot protect users against the ordering of transactions. Players such as miners, bots and validators can reorder various transactions and reap significant profits, called the Maximal Extractable Value (MEV). In this paper, we propose an MEV aware protocol design called Masquerade, and show that it will increase user satisfaction and confidence in the system.

arxiv-2311-09465.title: A new stabilized time-spectral finite element solver for fast simulation of blood flow
arxiv-2311-09465.creator: Mahdi Esmaily, Dongjie Jia
arxiv-2311-09465.description: Abstract The increasing application of cardiorespiratory simulations for diagnosis and surgical planning necessitates the development of computational methods significantly faster than the current technology. To achieve this objective, we leverage the time-periodic nature of these flows by discretizing equations in the frequency domain instead of the time domain.

arxiv-2409-18333.title: A Framework for Standardizing Similarity Measures in a Rapidly Evolving Field
arxiv-2409-18333.creator: Nathan Cloos, Guangyu Robert Yang, Christopher J. Cueva
arxiv-2409-18333.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nathan Cloos, Guangyu Robert Yang, Christopher J. Cueva. Similarity measures are fundamental tools for quantifying the alignment between artificial and biological systems. However, the diversity of similarity measures and their varied naming and implementation conventions makes it challenging to compare across studies. To facilitate comparisons and make explicit the implementation choices underlying a given code package, we have created and are continuing to develop a Python repository that benchmarks and standardizes similarity measures.

arxiv-2411-00649.title: Geometric Aspects to Diophantine Equations of the Form x 2 + z ​ x ​ y + y 2 = M x^{2}+zxy+y^{2}=M and z z -Rings
arxiv-2411-00649.creator: Chris Busenhart
arxiv-2411-00649.description: Abstract In the following we consider Diophantine equations of the form x 2 + z ​ x ​ y + y 2 = M x^{2}+zxy+y^{2}=M for given M , z ∈ ℤ M,z\in\mathbb{Z} and discuss the number of its (primitive) solutions as well as the construction of them.

arxiv-2508-12876.title: Comparison of three random field sampling methods for high-resolution Bayesian inversion with application to a plane stress problem Publication type: Paper
arxiv-2508-12876.creator: Pieter Vanmechelen 1,∗ \orcid 0000-0002-3733-2880, Geert Lombaert 2 \orcid 0000-0002-9273-3038 and Giovanni Samaey 1 \orcid 0000-0001-8433-4523
arxiv-2508-12876.description: Abstract Bayesian inversion aims to provide uncertainty quantification of posterior estimates conditional on observations. When the inferred parameter is a continuous spatial function, one common strategy is to model it as a random field. Several random field sampling strategies exist. In this article, we investigate three different approaches in terms of numerical efficiency and influence on the posterior distribution.

arxiv-2510-00744.title: Economic Bidding Strategy of Electric Vehicles in Real-Time Electricity Markets based on Marginal Opportunity Value
arxiv-2510-00744.creator: Zhen Zhu, Hongcai Zhang, Yonghua Song
arxiv-2510-00744.description: Abstract The participation of electric vehicle (EV) aggregators in real-time electricity markets offers promising revenue opportunities through price-responsive energy arbitrage. A central challenge in economic bidding lies in quantifying the marginal opportunity value of EVs’ charging and discharging decisions. This value is implicitly defined and dynamically shaped by uncertainties in electricity prices and availability of EV resources.

arxiv-2510-07662.title: Textual Entailment and Token Probability as Bias Evaluation Metrics
arxiv-2510-07662.creator: Virginia K. Felkner, Allison Lim, Jonathan May
arxiv-2510-07662.description: Abstract Measurement of social bias in language models is typically by token probability (TP) metrics, which are broadly applicable but have been criticized for their distance from real-world langugage model use cases and harms. In this work, we test natural language inference (NLI) as a more realistic alternative bias metric.

plos-pone-0010963.title: A Protein Phosphorylation Threshold for Functional Stacking of Plant Photosynthetic Membranes
plos-pone-0010963.creator: Rikard Fristedt, Pontus Granath, Alexander V. Vener
plos-pone-0010963.description: PLOS ONE research article. Phosphorylation of photosystem II (PSII) proteins affects macroscopic structure of thylakoid photosynthetic membranes in chloroplasts of the model plant Arabidopsis. In this study, light-scattering spectroscopy revealed that stacking of thylakoids isolated from wild type Arabidop

pmc-10648542.title: Lock-In Thermography with Cooling for the Inspection of Composite Materials
pmc-10648542.creator: Ryszard Dymitr Łukaszuk, Rafael Monteiro Marques, Tomasz Chady, Grzegorz Peruń, Tangbin Xia
pmc-10648542.description: This paper presents the development of the lock-in thermography system with an additional cooling system. System feasibility is tested by investigating a square-shaped glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) with artificially made outer flaws. The influence of heating mode and sinusoidal excitation period on the defect detectability is considered.

pmc-11397258.title: A Review of the Risk Factors Associated with Endometrial Hyperplasia During Perimenopause
pmc-11397258.creator: Lianping Wang, Wengong Wei, Meiling Cai
pmc-11397258.description: BackgroundEndometrial hyperplasia, characterized by excessive growth leading to endometrial thickening, is commonly observed in the premenopausal period. Its prevalence in postmenopausal women is approximately 15%, peaking between ages 50 and 60. This condition often manifests as abnormal uterine bleeding and can progress to malignancy, with varying risks depending on the type of hyperplasia.

pmc-11550882.title: Leveraging Quick Response Codes in Urology to Promote Patient Education While Contributing to Sustainable Healthcare Practices: A Retrospective Study
pmc-11550882.creator: Mohamed S Mohsin, Nader F Gaballa, Banan Osman, Ivo Dukic
pmc-11550882.description: BackgroundProviding patients with sufficient information about the planned procedure they will undergo, including the risks, benefits, and appropriate alternatives, forms a cornerstone of the high standards of care that a urologist provides. Our current standard for delivering information is printed patient information leaflets (PILs) following a consultation with a urologist in a clinic or via telemedicine.

pmc-11619196.title: Right Anterior Minithoracotomy Approach for Aortic Valve Replacement
pmc-11619196.creator: Ali Fatehi Hassanabad, Melissa A. King, Wojtek Karolak, Aleksander Dokollari, Aizel Castejon, Dominique de Waard, Holly N. Smith, Daniel D. Holloway, Corey Adams, William D. T. Kent
pmc-11619196.description: By sparing the sternum, the right anterior minithoracotomy (RAMT) approach may facilitate a quicker functional recovery when compared with conventional aortic valve replacement (AVR). In the following review, outcomes after RAMT AVR are compared with full sternotomy AVR. The RAMT approach is described, including suggestions for patient selection.

pmc-11675583.title: The Impact of Campylobacter, Salmonella, and Shigella in Diarrheal Infections in Central Africa (1998–2022): A Systematic Review
pmc-11675583.creator: Ornella Zong Minko, Rolande Mabika Mabika, Rachel Moyen, Franck Mounioko, Léonce Fauster Ondjiangui, Jean Fabrice Yala
pmc-11675583.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Gastric diseases caused, in particular, by Campylobacter, non-typhoidal Salmonella, and Shigella resulting from food and/or water problems, are a disproportionately distributed burden in developing countries in Central Africa. The aim of this work was to compile a list of studies establishing the prevalence of the involvement of these bacterial genera in diarrheal syndromes in Central Africa from 1998 to 2022.

pmc-11791991.title: Label-free electronic detection of peptide post-translational modification with functional enzyme-driven assay at the physical limit
pmc-11791991.creator: Eleonora Macchia, Kim Björkström, Amit Tewari, Ville Eskonen, Axel Luukkonen, Amir Mohammad Ghafari, Lucia Sarcina, Mariapia Caputo, Natalia Tong-Ochoa, Kari Kopra, Fredrik Pettersson, Zahra Gounani, Luisa Torsi, Harri Härmä, Ronald Österbacka
pmc-11791991.description: SummaryHigh-performance, ultra-sensitive, and universal protein post-translational modification (PTM) and protein-protein interaction (PPI) technologies are eagerly pursued in the pharmaceutical industry and bioanalytical research. Novel PTM and PPI detection methods outperform traditional assays in scope and scalability, enabling the collection of information on multiple biochemical targets.

pmc-12565229.title: Effective Conservative Management of Severe Scoliosis in a Girl with Prader–Willi Syndrome: A 20-Year Case Study Follow-Up
pmc-12565229.creator: Calogero Malfitano, Francesco Negrini, Valentina Palloni, Marcello Meggiolaro, Elena Brevi, Piero Benfatti, Fabio Zaina, Giorgio Ferriero, Stefano Negrini, Alan H Daniels
pmc-12565229.description: Background: Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare syndrome that presents in about 1 in 25,000 newborns. It is characterized by a typical phenotype that includes short stature, hypothyroidism and hypogonadism, cognitive and developmental delays, slow growth, obesity, and, in most patients, scoliosis.

pmc-12622746.title: Exploring the mechanism of Stephania tetrandra S. Moore in the treatment of cisplatin resistance against ovarian cancer through integration of network pharmacology and molecular docking
pmc-12622746.creator: Yuanyuan Zhong, Shanshan Cai, Chunyue Fang, Wei Dai
pmc-12622746.description: Cisplatin resistance is a major contributor to treatment failure in ovarian cancer (OC). This study investigates the mechanisms of action and therapeutic targets of Stephania tetrandra S. Moorefor cisplatin-resistant OC. OC datasets were obtained from the gene expression omnibus database, and differentially expressed genes were identified through weighted gene co-expression network analysis.

pmc-12719259.title: A novel approach for proton therapy pencil beam scanning patient specific quality assurance using an integrated detector system and 3D dose reconstruction
pmc-12719259.creator: Joseph J. Bateman, Sonia Escribano-Rodriguez, Samuel Flynn, Tony Price, Raffaella Radogna, Saad Shaikh, Harry Barnett, Connor Godden, Matthew Warren, Febian, Catherine Burne, Alison Warry, Lee Harrison-Carey, Colin Baker, Simon Jolly
pmc-12719259.description: PurposeCurrent proton beam therapy patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA) methods rely on time-intensive phantom measurements or machine-reported parameters without independent verification. This work presents an integrated detector system for phantom-less Pencil Beam Scanning (PBS) PSQA, providing independent spot-by-spot measurements of all critical beam parameters and 3D dose reconstruction.

pmc-13556631.title: 667. Neurotherapies for ADHD: do they work?
pmc-13556631.creator: K Rubia, A Conti, N Bhozilova, I Eraydim, L Johansson, P Santosh, D Stringer, B Carter, S Cortese
pmc-13556631.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundStimulant medications are effective for ADHD. However, they have side effects, unknown longer-term effects, poor adherence and are not preferred by children and their parents.
